output.title: Measuring counting rules starts with one workflow
output.body:
If you want to measure counting rules, start with one recurring workflow instead of the abstract idea of “counting” in general.

Pick the place where your team already counts something by hand: invoices to review, leads to qualify, stock to reconcile, or tickets to close. Then write down four things in plain English: what is being counted, who checks it, what rule decides a pass or fail, and what happens when the count is wrong.

That last point matters. A count only becomes useful when you know the control around it. If a mistake can be reversed later, that is one kind of workflow. If the count leads to payment, approval, or another high-risk decision, human sign-off stays in place.

The practical next step is simple: write one page for a single workflow with the count, the rule, the owner, and one recent error. If the rule is repeatable and the outcome is measurable, it is worth looking at automation support. If the rule depends on judgment, keep the human in the loop. That is usually the part where the spreadsheet gets tired first.
